title: HUL Interim Dividend 2026: What Investors Need to Know
description: Hindustan Unilever (HUL) has declared an interim dividend of ₹19 per equity share for 2026. This payout represents 1,900% of the company's face value of ₹1 pe.

faq.a: An interim dividend is a dividend paid by a company during its financial year, before the final annual results are declared. It's usually based on the company's performance in the first half or three quarters of the year.

faq.q: How is HUL's dividend of 1,900% of face value calculated?
faq.a: The face value of HUL's equity share is ₹1. A dividend of 1,900% means 19 times the face value. So, 19 * ₹1 = ₹19 per equity share.

faq.q: Do I need to pay tax on HUL's dividend?
faq.a: Yes, for resident Indian individuals, dividend income is added to your total income and taxed at your applicable income tax slab rates. TDS may also be deducted by the company if the dividend exceeds ₹5,000 in a financial year.

faq.q: What happens if I buy HUL shares on the ex-dividend date?
faq.a: If you buy HUL shares on or after the ex-dividend date, you will not be eligible to receive the announced interim dividend. You must purchase the shares before the ex-dividend date.

faq.q: When will the HUL dividend be credited to my account?
faq.a: The company typically announces a payment date along with the dividend declaration and record date. Dividends are usually credited directly to the bank account linked to your demat account within 30 days of the declaration.
